value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for thumbnail and title candidates, checked for small sizes and honesty, tested by plan and picked by a person
value.lets_workers: Draft title and thumbnail candidates for a video from what it actually shows, check every candidate's text at the small sizes people see it, its contrast and its honesty, with no claim or promise the video does not deliver, set candidates side by side for a person to pick, and write an A/B plan with its decision rule fixed in advance for a person to run in the platform's own test tool.

flow.when: Three to six titles from what the video shows.
Text size at each display size, word count and contrast.
Every claim traced; no banned pattern; every promise kept.
The candidates that pass, side by side in a recorded shuffle.
A person picks one, or none.
An A/B plan fixed before any result.
The person records what the platform's test reported and the decision.

value.worked_example: Synthetic: three thumbnails and three titles for a fictional pantry's film. The size check finds one cover's text under 12 CSS px on both small displays, the contrast fixture shows its grey text fails the normal-text ratio that applies once it is that small, the title checks reject a clickbait title, and the A/B plan compares the two good covers by the platform's own measure.
value.complements: The taste palettes pack shows options side by side and keeps a person's choice; this pack makes the candidates, checks them and plans the test. The video review pack's claim trace is what the honesty check reads.
provenance_notes: Generalizes the cover and title practice of a working short-form video studio: a designed cover with the hook line rather than a random mid-video frame, covers that never give away a reveal, alt text for people who read rather than watch, honest hook words over keyword scores, and A/B tests of hook wording and covers run by a person.

value.title: Small-size rules for thumbnails
value.category_reason: A zero-call procedure using the video QA pack's legibility and contrast code.
rules: List the display widths the platform shows the thumbnail at; a card, a list row and a small row are typical.
Text's size at each width is its pixel size in the master times the display width over the master width; it must reach 12 CSS px at the smallest.
Five words or fewer on a thumbnail; one focal subject; nothing important under the platform's own overlays, such as a duration badge.
Text and its panel meet WCAG contrast, 4.5 to 1, or 3 to 1 for large text, unrounded.
A frame candidate is a designed frame, never a half-shown caption or a mid-transition frame.
value.layout_note: A designed cover rendered from a layout can also go through the screenshot design review pack, which measures text size, contrast and cropping from its layout facts with the same 12 px floor.

value.title: Honesty rules for titles and thumbnails
value.category_reason: A zero-call procedure: a fixed pattern and a trace lookup.
rules: Every claim in a title or on a thumbnail is a claim the video's claim trace upholds, with its qualifier where the trace has one.
No banned pattern: the regular expression below, which a requester may extend but never shorten.
The title is a question the video answers or a plain statement of what it shows; the promise names the moment that keeps it.
No all-capital titles, and no superlative without evidence.
Generated imagery on a cover is labeled as generated.
value.banned_pattern: (?i)(you won't believe|shocking|insane|nobody (knows|tells)|everyone is|doctors hate|this one trick|gone wrong|\b(must|need to) see\b)

value.title: A/B plan rules
value.category_reason: A zero-call procedure for planning a test whose decision is fixed in advance.
rules: Change one thing: the thumbnail, the title, or both as one pair, never several at once.
Two or three variants, the most one platform's built-in test accepts at the time of writing.
Fix the metric, the minimum duration, the decision rule and what counts as no difference before any result exists.
Use the measure the platform's own test reports; one platform picks by watch time, not by clicks.
A person starts the test, reads its result and records the decision; nothing else touches the published video.
